Use case / workload
- Primary: internal customer support agent + call summarization for QA/compliance; content is sensitive (PII). Needs strong access controls + auditability.

Key requirements (from calls + security questionnaire)
Data residency
- “EU-only means EU-only” (verbatim from security lead). No processing/storage outside EU.
- Wants written confirmation of regions used, backup/DR posture, and any cross-region replication.

Retention controls (deal-critical)
- Wants tenant-configurable retention by data type (not one blanket setting).
- Proposed defaults they asked us to support as configurable options:
  - Audit logs: 365 days (minimum)
  - Admin activity / configuration changes: 365 days preferred
  - Inference request metadata (non-payload): 90 days baseline; option for 30 days
  - Telemetry/analytics: 30–90 days (they want option to reduce)
- Legal hold: must be supported with documented workflow (“we need to be able to freeze deletions during investigations”).
- Needs evidence that retention is enforced (not just policy text): effective policy view + last enforcement run + exceptions list.

Audit logging + exports
- Must export audit logs to Splunk (preferred) and/or S3-compatible storage.
- Needs clarity on what happens if they request an export beyond retention window (expectation: not available; should be explicit in export metadata).
- Asked whether exports can be scoped by time range and event type; also asked for schema stability / versioning.

Security controls
- SSO/SAML required (Okta). SCIM is a plus (not listed as hard req yet).
- Encryption: KMS integration / BYOK strongly preferred; asked about HSM-backed keys (future).
- RBAC: wants separation between platform admins and audit readers.

Commercial/procurement
- They are comparing against Azure OpenAI + Bedrock; motivation for Redwood is tighter performance economics + dedicated isolation + private deployment option.
- Procurement wants retention language in MSA/DPA to align with internal policy (no “indefinite retention”).
